summary: Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs says Croatia has applied the Schengen rules in full since 1 January 2023, and that third-country nationals, whether or not they need a visa, can stay in the Schengen Area up to 90 days in any 180-day period. EU nationals travel freely with a passport or ID card; nationals of the countries on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806) need no visa (the ETIAS travel authorisation is not yet in operation), and others need a Schengen short-stay visa costing EUR 90.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area: Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs says third-country nationals, whether or not they need a visa, may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and that time spent in Croatia is added to time spent in the other Schengen states. The remaining days can be checked with the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) web tool.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of Croatia — Visas (calculating time spent in the Schengen area)

fee.notes: Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs waives the fee for children up to 12, close family members of Croatian citizens, family members of EEA and Swiss citizens travelling with them, pupils, students and accompanying teachers travelling to study, and researchers, among others; the Visa Code otherwise sets EUR 45 for children aged 6 to 11.

fee.text: Applicants shall pay a visa fee of EUR 90.

processing.text: That period may be extended up to a maximum of 45 calendar days in individual cases, notably when further scrutiny of the application is needed.

stayDays.text: This Regulation establishes the procedures and conditions for issuing visas for intended stays on the territory of the Member States not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

extendable.text: The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa shall be extended where the competent authority of a Member State considers that a visa holder has provided proof of force majeure or humanitarian reasons preventing him from leaving the territory of the Member States before the expiry of the period of validity of or the duration of stay authorised by the visa.

method.text: An application shall be examined and decided on by the consulate of the competent Member State in whose jurisdiction the applicant legally resides.

applyWindow.text: The EU Visa Code says an application is lodged no more than six months before the start of the visit and, as a rule, no later than 15 calendar days before it; in justified urgent cases the consulate may accept it later.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Croatia: Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs says time spent in Croatia is added to time spent in the other Schengen states.

The UK government's travel advice says EES registration may take each passenger extra time, so be prepared to wait longer than usual at the border and allow more time for immigration controls when you leave the Schengen area.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Croatia?
faq.answer: No. The United States is on the EU's list of countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS starts, visa-exempt travellers will need this travel authorisation (EUR 20 application fee) to enter.

faq.question: Is Croatia in the Schengen Area and does it use the euro?
faq.answer: Yes to both. Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs says Croatia has applied the Schengen rules in full since 1 January 2023, and Canada's travel advice says the currency of Croatia is the euro. Border checks can still happen: the UK government says there are checks at Slovenia's borders with Croatia, and Canada says member states may temporarily reintroduce controls at internal border crossings.

faq.question: How much does a Croatia Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs EUR 90; Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs exempts children up to the age of 12 from the fee. Third-country nationals can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen Area, and the EU Visa Code says applications are decided within 15 calendar days, extendable to a maximum of 45 in individual cases.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Croatia?
faq.answer: ETIAS is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once it starts, Croatia will be among the 30 countries that require visa-exempt travellers to hold an ETIAS travel authorisation, with an application fee of EUR 20.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Croatia without a visa?
faq.answer: Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs says third-country nationals, whether or not they need a visa, can stay in the Schengen Area up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and that time spent in Croatia is added to time spent in the other Schengen states.
